purpose: Move a query point and separate its membership, the existence of some neighborhood, the fit of one chosen neighborhood and openness of the whole set.
meaning: A set in a metric space is open when every point of the set has a positive-radius open ball contained in it. That condition concerns the existence of some sufficiently small ball, not whether one currently chosen radius fits. A closed disk has interior points too, but its included rim points have no positive ball contained in the disk.

definition.setting: Euclidean neighborhoods around points on the horizontal diameter of a radius-two disk in the ambient plane ℝ².

signature.‖p‖: Distance from p to the origin.
signature.C(x): Signed clearance to the disk boundary.
signature.b: Selected open or closed disk boundary.

conditions: The ambient space is ℝ² with Euclidean distance. U is either the disk ‖z‖<2 cm or the disk ‖z‖≤2 cm; p=(x,0) has x between −3 and 3 cm.
The selected neighborhood Bε(p) is an open ball, using strict distance less than ε. The live radius lies from 0.05 to 1.5 cm; radius zero is excluded.
Point membership is strict at the open disk rim and inclusive at the closed disk rim. An interior point, for either disk, has |x|<2 and positive clearance.
The chosen open ball fits when |x|+ε≤2, including equality even for the open disk. At tangency the touching point is excluded from the inner open ball.

For an interior point, the constructive radius C(x)/2 is positive and works, even when it is below the live slider minimum. Failure of the selected radius does not imply absence of every possible radius.
Global openness depends on the whole selected set, not this point or radius. In general a set may be both open and closed, or neither; the two labels are not universal opposites.
definition.domain_notes: The primary output is signed clearance, which may be positive, zero or negative. It is not a radius or an openness truth value. The disk boundary choice, point membership, interior status and chosen-ball containment are four separate notions.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Choose the open or closed disk of radius 2 cm, and p=(x,0) with horizontal coordinate measured in centimetres. The selected neighborhood is the open ball Bε(p) of positive radius ε. Its signed clearance is C(x)=2−|x| cm. For either disk choice, Bε(p) is contained exactly when |x|+ε≤2. A positive contained ball exists exactly when |x|<2; the full open disk is open, while the full closed disk is not open in ℝ².
grammar.precedence: First distinguish the selected set and point. Then compare the chosen radius with clearance; keep that one-ball containment test separate from existence of some positive ball and the global openness condition.

prompts.prompt: Can the set remain open while this chosen neighborhood fails?
prompts.answer: Yes. An interior point admits a sufficiently small positive radius even if a larger selected radius extends outside the set.

prompts.prompt: Does a closed disk have interior points?
prompts.answer: Yes. Points strictly inside the rim admit positive contained balls. The included rim points prevent the entire closed disk from being open in ℝ².
